problem_statement: Extend the CBOR reader API with cbor_skip_next() to advance past any CBOR object regardless of type, plus cbor_get_position() and cbor_get_remaining() accessors, and cover the extensions with new unit tests.

verification.reason: The statement names all three functions (cbor_skip_next, cbor_get_position, cbor_get_remaining), describes the required behavior (advance past any CBOR object regardless of type; position and remaining accessors), and the error handling, return types, and per-type behavior checked by the tests are natural consequences that a competent developer would implement. problem_statement_fixed: Extend the CBOR reader API (os/lib/cbor.h, os/lib/cbor.c) with three functions that take the reader state. `bool cbor_skip_next(cbor_reader_state_t *state)` advances the reader past the next complete CBOR data item of any major type: unsigned and negative integers with any argument width, byte and text strings, simple values (false, true, null, undefined and one-byte simple values), half-, single- and double-precision floats, and arrays and maps, which are skipped together with all of their elements, including nested arrays and maps. It works at the top level and inside an array or map whose header has already been read (skipping the last element of such an array or map completes it, as reading that element would), and it returns true when it skipped an item. It returns false when there is no item to skip (empty input) or the item cannot be skipped: its argument bytes or string payload extend past the end of the input, an array or map contains fewer encoded elements than its header declares, or the initial byte is the break stop code (0xff) or uses a reserved additional-information value. `const uint8_t *cbor_get_position(cbor_reader_state_t *state)` returns a pointer to the reader's current position in the input buffer, and `size_t cbor_get_remaining(cbor_reader_state_t *state)` returns the number of input bytes not yet consumed. After a successful skip, the position has advanced by exactly the item's encoded length and the remaining count has gone down by the same amount.
